Freeport-McMoRan stock: Freeport agrees to buy Aurora West stake
sum: Freeport-McMoRan agreed on Thursday, November 12, to acquire an initial 51% interest in the Aurora West project in British Columbia for C$110 million in cash at closing. The transaction gives the copper producer a new exploration position while leaving completion subject to customary conditions, including approval from the TSX Venture Exchange.
According to the TDG Gold announcement, Freeport will initially own 51% of each joint venture company holding the relevant Aurora West claims. TDG will retain 49% of Aurora West JVCo after closing.

Freeport also receives an earn-in option. It can increase its interest in Aurora West JVCo to 75% by funding C$80 million of additional exploration expenditure. A separate option would allow Freeport to acquire 100% of ClaimsCo for a further C$40 million payment.

Freeport committed to fund C$30 million of exploration expenditure within three years after closing, including at least C$15 million during the first two years. The reorganization is expected in December 2026, with closing scheduled five business days after the required conditions are satisfied or waived.

The agreement follows Freeport's November 4 approval of a 4.5-billion-dollar Bagdad expansion in Arizona. In its company release, Freeport said the project is intended to add long-term copper and molybdenum production, with initial output targeted for mid-2030.

Freeport-McMoRan stock: Bagdad plan adds U.S. copper growth
sum: Freeport-McMoRan is advancing its U.S. copper strategy after the board approved the Bagdad expansion in Arizona on November 4, 2026. The company said in its Freeport-McMoRan news release that the brownfield program is designed to more than double mining and milling rates at the long-running operation.

Bagdad's long-term annual copper production is expected to exceed 400 million pounds, including an incremental 225 million pounds. Molybdenum output is projected to top 20 million pounds a year, with an incremental 12 million pounds. Freeport said the expanded mine would become the second-largest copper operation in the United States behind Morenci.

The plan includes a new concentrator with about 115,000 tons per day of additional processing capacity, plus a primary crusher, overland conveyor, water pipeline, power line and mining equipment. Bagdad has operated since 1945 and completed its conversion to a fully autonomous haulage fleet in 2025.

Construction is expected to take about three and a half years, with initial production targeted for mid-2030. Freeport plans to classify the capital spending as discretionary and expects about 20 percent of project costs in 2027, 30 to 35 percent in 2028 and the balance in 2029 and 2030.

The company expects modern technology, automation, economies of scale and molybdenum by-product credits to reduce long-term unit net cash costs by about 20 percent. For investors, the potential production increase must therefore be weighed against a large multiyear funding requirement, cost escalation risk and the long wait for additional volumes.

Freeport-McMoRan stock: $4.5 billion Bagdad expansion approved
sum: Freeport-McMoRan's board approved a $4.5 billion expansion and modernization program for the Bagdad copper and molybdenum operation in Arizona on Wednesday, November 4, the company said in a Freeport-McMoRan news release. The brownfield project is designed to more than double Bagdad's mining and milling rates and strengthen the miner's US copper growth strategy.

Freeport expects the mine to produce more than 400 million pounds of copper a year in the long term, including roughly 225 million pounds of incremental output. Molybdenum production is projected to exceed 20 million pounds annually, an increase of about 12 million pounds. Those figures describe planned output after the expansion rather than near-term production.

The project will add concentrator facilities with approximately 115,000 tons per day of incremental nameplate processing capacity. Supporting infrastructure includes a primary crusher, an overland conveyor, water and power systems, mining equipment and related facilities. Freeport said the plan will use Bagdad's existing infrastructure, reserve base and operating workforce.

Engineering, procurement planning and early works are under way. Construction is expected to take approximately three and a half years, with initial incremental production targeted for mid-2030. Freeport expects about 20 percent of project costs to be funded in 2027, 30 to 35 percent in 2028 and the balance in 2029 and 2030. The company said the spending will be incorporated into its updated capital expenditure outlook and treated as discretionary under its financial policy.

The company estimates a reduction of approximately 20 percent in long-term unit net cash costs. Management attributes the expected improvement to economies of scale, modern technology, automation and molybdenum by-product credits. The project economics are supported at a copper price of approximately $4.00 per pound and a molybdenum price of $20 per pound, according to the release.

Freeport said the expansion would make Bagdad the second-largest copper mine in the United States, behind its Morenci operation, and a leading US molybdenum producer. The mine has operated since 1945 and has a current reserve life exceeding 80 years before additional mineral resources are considered.

sum: Freeport-McMoRan reported stronger third-quarter earnings on October 27, 2026, as higher copper prices offset lower sales volumes during the recovery of its Grasberg operation in Indonesia. The Northern Miner reported that revenue rose 8% to 7.55 billion US dollars and net income attributable to common shareholders increased to 1.17 billion US dollars from 674 million US dollars a year earlier.

Freeport-McMoRan stock traded at 56.71 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:40 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. The real-time quote of Freeport-McMoRan stock provides the latest trading reference for investors.

Adjusted earnings, which exclude 101 million US dollars in net charges, reached 88 cents per share and exceeded analyst expectations, according to The Northern Miner. Reported diluted earnings were 81 cents per share, compared with 46 cents in the third quarter of 2025.

The improvement came despite copper sales falling to 749 million pounds from 977 million pounds a year earlier. Freeport's realized copper price increased to 6.54 US dollars per pound from 4.68 US dollars, helping to offset the lower volumes. Quarterly copper production was 832 million pounds, with inventory accounting for part of the gap between production and sales.

Freeport reduced its consolidated copper-sales forecast to 3.0 billion pounds for 2026 from 3.1 billion pounds in its July forecast. The 2027 estimate fell to 3.7 billion pounds from 3.8 billion pounds, while the 2028 outlook remained 4.1 billion pounds. The company attributed the changes to lower operating rates in the United States and Chile and to updated mine plans.

The phased Grasberg restart remains the central driver of Freeport's volume outlook. The operation ran at 67% of capacity in the third quarter, up from earlier recovery levels, and mining rates at the Grasberg Block Cave averaged about 70,000 tonnes per day, compared with 53,000 tonnes in the second quarter.

Freeport expects Grasberg to reach 80% of capacity by mid-2027 and approach full capacity by the end of that year. Material-handling upgrades are scheduled for completion in early 2027, while preparations continue for a restart of Production Block 1S around mid-2027.

The Northern Miner reported that revenue rose 8 percent to USD 7.55 billion, while net income attributable to common shareholders reached USD 1.17 billion, or USD 0.81 per diluted share, compared with USD 674 million, or USD 0.46, a year earlier.

Adjusted earnings were USD 1.28 billion, or USD 0.88 per share, after the company excluded USD 101 million in net charges related mainly to idle facilities and recovery and restoration work. Operating cash flow increased to USD 1.98 billion from USD 1.69 billion. Higher realized copper prices helped offset lower sales volumes during the recovery of the Grasberg Block Cave in Indonesia.

Freeport sold 749 million pounds of copper in the quarter, down from 977 million pounds a year earlier, while production reached 832 million pounds. The realized copper price rose to USD 6.54 per pound from USD 4.68, according to The Northern Miner. Unit net cash costs nevertheless increased to USD 2.07 per pound from USD 1.40, excluding the separately reported idle-facility, direct recovery and restoration costs.

Management now expects consolidated copper sales of 3.0 billion pounds in 2026 and 3.7 billion pounds in 2027, down from earlier forecasts of 3.1 billion and 3.8 billion pounds. The 2028 estimate remains 4.1 billion pounds. Freeport attributed the reductions to lower production in the United States and Chile and to updated mine plans.

The phased Grasberg restart is still the main source of expected volume growth. Mining rates at the Grasberg Block Cave averaged about 70,000 tonnes per day in the third quarter, up from 53,000 tonnes in the second quarter. The operation reached 67 percent of mine capacity during the quarter.

Freeport is targeting 80 percent of capacity by mid-2027 and near-full capacity by the end of 2027. Material-handling upgrades for the automated rail system are scheduled to finish around the end of 2026 or early 2027, while preparations for the restart of Production Block 1S are advancing toward mid-2027. Limited water availability remains a constraint on higher milling rates, although the company said the impact has so far been limited.

sum: A single policy update with no operational content just sent the entire copper mining sector into freefall, erasing billions in gains that took months to build. Here is why tariff uncertainty can reprice a whole industry inside minutes.

Shares of Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE:FCX | FCX Price Prediction) are sliding early Thursday as a record rally in copper reverses inside a single session. Freeport-McMoRan stock is down 8% to $70.43 after reports cast doubt on the refined-copper tariffs that had powered the metal to fresh highs earlier this week. The scarcity trade that built up all summer is unwinding in real time, and copper miners are traveling with it.

The selloff runs deep across the group. Also under pressure, Southern Copper (NYSE:SCCO) stock is down 7% to $195.66, and Teck Resources (NYSE:TECK) stock is down 7% to $65.08. Both names had ridden the same setup that lifted the group into Tuesday’s records, and both are now handing back a meaningful piece of that move.

The Global X Copper Miners ETF (NYSEARCA:COPX) is down 7% as the entire basket rerates in unison, with its three largest U.S.-listed constituents leading the decline. Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.41%, so today’s damage is concentrated in copper names rather than the wider market.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange is down 3.1% to $14,312 per metric ton after touching a record $14,875 earlier in the same session. The reversal followed reports that the White House hasn’t yet reached a decision on tariffs covering refined copper, with officials weighing how higher prices would feed through into manufacturing costs. Precious metals are lower too, with a firmer dollar and higher inflation-adjusted Treasury yields weighing on the broader metals complex.

Expectations of tariff action had been a central plank of the rally, pulling U.S.-bound metal out of global warehouses and building a scarcity premium into the physical price. Remove that expectation, and the premium unwinds inside minutes, which is why a policy update with no operational content just repriced the entire mining group.

sum: The Grasberg copper and gold mine located in Papua, Indonesia (Orbital Horizon/Gallo Images via Getty Images)
The harder test will be downstreaming, decarbonisation and Papuan equity.
Indonesia and the US mining giant Freeport-McMoRan have struck an agreement extending the operating rights of the vast copper and gold complex in Papua for the life of its reserves.

The memorandum of understanding signed last week amends the special mining permit for the Grasberg mine, operated by PT Freeport Indonesia (PTFI), preserves the existing governance structure, and sets out commitments for expanded exploration spending, social investments in Papua, including a hospital and medical education facilities, continued prioritisation of domestic downstreaming, and an eventual additional 12% equity transfer to the Indonesian state. Freeport will retain 48.76% ownership, declining to roughly 37% after 2042.

On paper, the arrangement signals stability and long-term partnership. In practice, it raises deeper questions about sovereignty over strategic minerals, industrial policy and the unresolved tensions surrounding West Papua.

Grasberg is not just another mine. It is one of the world’s largest copper and gold reserves. Copper is indispensable for electric vehicles, renewable power grids and digital infrastructure. As major economies scramble to secure critical mineral supply chains, copper has become a geopolitical asset.

Indonesia’s push for greater state participation in PTFI has always had two objectives: increase national revenue and ensure compliance with downstreaming – the requirement that minerals be processed domestically rather than exported as raw ore. Downstreaming is meant to generate higher value-added activity at home: refining, manufacturing, skilled employment and technological spillovers.

Billionaire mining executive Robert Friedland addressed the USC Marshall Energy Business Summit back in September to outline the severe global copper supply crisis. Driven by rising demand from electrification, renewable energy infrastructure, data centers, artificial intelligence (AI) development, and grid upgrades, Friedland contrasted the vast oil market with the smaller, thinly traded metals markets, including copper. He noted that shifting away from crude oil requires these metals for electric vehicles, windmills, solar panels, and military technology. Over the past 10,000 years, humanity has mined about 700 million metric tons of copper, with 80% still in use today. Friedland warned of a “train wreck” unless six new tier-one mines come online every year from now until 2050, representing 40% of future production. I've used the plural to illustrate that there are two key copper prices that investors follow and to highlight a bullish point for Freeport. There are the Commodity Exchange (COMEX) price in the U.S. and the London Metal Exchange (LME) price used internationally. The good news is that both are trading close to their all-time highs.

It might seem obvious that COMEX and LME copper prices should trade in sync; after all, copper is a commodity product. However, the reality is that a significant spread existed between the two in 2025, as the market bid up COMEX prices in anticipation of tariffs on imported copper by the Trump administration. Indeed, the COMEX/LME copper price spread reached almost 30% in the summer.

Both copper prices are now close to all-time highs, with the COMEX price currently around $5.65 per pound, up from $4.10 a year ago. That's more supportive for Freeport, as it indicates strength in underlying demand rather than U.S. inventory stockpiling ahead of potential tariffs.

That said, Freeport is not yet fully able to take advantage because the company suffered a tragic, fatal accident in an Indonesian mine, which has reduced its production expectations for 2025 and 2026. sum: The mining space has had a banner year in 2025, courtesy of a dramatic rally in commodities. Gold staged a record-setting upswing as investors flocked to traditional havens amid economic, geopolitical and tariff-related uncertainties. Copper and silver prices have also hit record levels amid rising demand and a supply crisis.

Surging commodities prices improved miners' cash flow and created optionality for investment in project acceleration and enhanced shareholder returns. Gold prices have seen an unprecedented rally this year, mainly attributable to aggressive trade policies, including sweeping new import tariffs announced by President Donald Trump that have intensified global trade tensions and heightened investor anxiety. Also, central banks worldwide have been accumulating gold reserves, led by risks arising from Trump's policies.

The Federal Reserve's interest rate reduction, hopes of more rate cuts amid concerns over the labor market and an economic slowdown, along with concerns over a protracted U.S. government shutdown, have contributed to the record-setting rally, driving bullion prices north of $4,000 per ton for the first time. Increased purchases by central banks and geopolitical and trade tensions are the other factors expected to help the yellow metal sustain the upswing in gold prices. Prices of copper, the backbone of electrification, have been volatile yet mostly favorable this year due to global economic and trade uncertainties. Freeport plans to restore large-scale production at Grasberg in Q2 2026
sum: Freeport McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) says it plans to restore large-scale production at Indonesia’s Grasberg minerals district from the second quarter of 2026, following a fatal incident that halted operations earlier this year.

On Sept. 8, a catastrophic mudslide released 800,000 metric tons of wet material into Grasberg’s Block Cave underground mine, resulting in the death of seven workers. Since then, Freeport has declared force majeure and completed an investigation into the incident, the details of which are yet to be disclosed.

Remediation activities are currently being advanced to prepare for a phased restart and ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine beginning in Q2 2026, the US copper mining giant said in a press release on Tuesday.

Freeport has already resumed activities at the Deep Mill Level Zone and Big Gossan underground mines, which it said were not affected by the mud flow. Together with the Block Cave, they form one of the world’s largest copper-gold mine complexes, producing 1.7 billion lb. of copper and 1.4 million oz. of gold annually. The Grasberg district is situated in the remote highlands of the Sudirman Mountains in Central Papua.
Freeport serves as Grasberg’s operator and holds an approximate 49% interest, while the rest is owned by the Indonesian government.

“We have incorporated the learnings from the recent tragic incident into our future plans and are implementing several initiatives to address the conditions that led to the incident,” Freeport’s chief executive Kathleen Quirk said in the Tuesday press release.

According to Freeport, Grasberg’s in 2026 production will be similar to 2025 at about 1 billion lb. of copper and 900,000 oz. of gold — about 35% lower than its pre-incident estimates following a September revision.
